answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with a reputation orchard: every new agent starts with a tiny transaction limit and must earn trust by completing verifiable tasks attested by established peers. Reputation grows slowly, like trees maturing, and is tied to a public history of useful work, not to a self-declared name. Creating many fake accounts gains nothing, because each one starts at the same low horizon and must pay the same time and work cost before it can transact at scale. A nebula of new identities cannot merge scores, so an attacker faces the full cost once per identity.
